# Kyoto Spring Trip Overview

A 4-day Kyoto plan for **2 adults** from **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-13**, built around **temples, local food, light hiking, and one traditional cultural experience**.
I’ve kept the route **knee-friendly**, minimized long stair-heavy walks, and aimed for **3-star or better lodging near transit** within your **$2,400 total budget** excluding international flights.

# 4-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Budget Plan

## Day 1 — Arrival, Gion, and Riverside Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive in Kyoto, check in near Kyoto Station or Gojo Station, and rest after travel.
- Afternoon: Easy start at **Kiyomizu-dera area only from the lower approach if energy is good**; otherwise focus on **Gion, Hanamikoji, and Yasaka Shrine** for flat walking.
- Dinner: Kyoto-style set meal with **yudofu** or **obanzai** near Gion.
- Knee-friendly note: Skip steep side lanes and keep taxi rides between Kyoto Station, Gion, and hotel if needed.

## Day 2 — Arashiyama, Bamboo Grove, and Scenic Temple Stops
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Early train to **Arashiyama**; visit the **Bamboo Grove** and **Togetsukyo Bridge** with short, flat walks.
- Afternoon: Choose one gentle temple stop such as **Tenryu-ji gardens**; avoid extended hillside routes and keep pace flexible.
- Dinner: Try **tofu cuisine** or **soba** in Arashiyama or back near central Kyoto.
- Knee-friendly note: Use the main paths only; skip steep detours and long stair climbs.

## Day 3 — Fushimi Inari, Tea Culture, and Traditional Experience
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- Morning: Visit **Fushimi Inari Taisha** early and stay on the lower shrine area rather than attempting the full mountain loop.
- Afternoon: Head to **Uji** for **matcha desserts** and a relaxed riverside stroll, or return to Kyoto for a **tea ceremony**.
- Dinner: Kaiseki-lite or a seasonal Kyoto dinner set in central Kyoto.
- Traditional experience: Book a **tea ceremony** in a central, accessible venue with seated format.

## Day 4 — Northern Kyoto Temples and Departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Visit **Kinkaku-ji** for a highlight temple stop; use taxis or buses to reduce walking strain.
- Afternoon: If time allows, add **Nijo Castle** for an easier, flatter cultural visit before departure.
- Dinner: Final meal near Kyoto Station before heading out.
- Knee-friendly note: Keep this day transport-light and avoid stacking too many temple grounds.

## Cost Plan for 2 Adults

| Category | Estimate (USD) | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Lodging, 3 nights | 540 | 3-star or better, transit-friendly area |
| Local transport | 120 | Subway, bus, occasional taxi |
| Food and drinks | 520 | Mix of casual meals, one nicer dinner, snacks |
| Admissions and cultural activity | 220 | Temples, castle, tea ceremony |
| Local shopping / buffer | 180 | Small extras, transit top-ups |
| Contingency | 220 | Price swings, taxi backup, flexibility |
| Total | **1,800** | Leaves about **$600** cushion |

## Lodging Fit Near Transit

| Area | Why it works | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Kyoto Station | Best transit access, easy arrivals/departures, many 3-star hotels | Convenience and knee-friendly logistics |
| Gojo | Central but quieter, good subway access | Balanced sightseeing base |
| Karasuma / Shijo | Strong restaurant access, easy bus/subway links | Food-focused travelers |
| Gion edge / Higashiyama lower area | Atmospheric, but choose carefully for stairs | If you want charm with controlled walking |

## Packing Checklist for Kyoto in April

- Light layers: long-sleeve tops, cardigan, light jacket
- Comfortable walking shoes with cushioning
- Foldable umbrella or compact rain shell
- Socks you can remove easily for temple visits
- Small day bag with water bottle and tissues
- Portable phone charger
- Knee support item if already used: brace, sleeve, or compression wrap
- Basic meds: pain relief, blister care, any prescriptions
- Cash and card mix; some small places still prefer cash
- Reusable bag for snacks or purchases
- Camera or phone with extra storage for cherry blossom season
